name: CALCULATION (STRATEGY SOLITAIRE)
description: Calculation (also known as Strategy or 'Broken Intervals') is a unique solitaire card game that deviates from standard 'Klondike' mechanics. Unlike most solitaires that build in simple 1-2-3 steps, each of the four foundation piles in Calculation builds at a different mathematical interval: Pile 1 goes 1, 2, 3...; Pile 2 goes 2, 4, 6...; Pile 3 goes 3, 6, 9...; and Pile 4 goes 4, 8, Q... It is a game of pure skill and memory where the layout of the 'Waste' piles determines victory.

content.text: Calculation (also known as Strategy or 'Broken Intervals') is a unique solitaire card game that deviates from standard 'Klondike' mechanics. Unlike most solitaires that build in simple 1-2-3 steps, each of the four foundation piles in Calculation builds at a different mathematical interval: Pile 1 goes 1, 2, 3...; Pile 2 goes 2, 4, 6...; Pile 3 goes 3, 6, 9...; and Pile 4 goes 4, 8, Q... It is a game of pure skill and memory where the layout of the 'Waste' piles determines victory.

Developed as a mental exercise in the early 20th century. It was popularized by the legendary card experts Albert H. Morehead and Geoffrey Mott-Smith in their seminal book 'The Complete Book of Solitaire'.
One player (solitaire). The game is played by a single player who turns cards from the stock and builds the four foundations or places cards on the four waste (tableau) piles.
52 cards. Remove one Ace, one 2, one 3, and one 4. Place them as the base of 4 Foundation piles.
52 cards. Remove one Ace, one 2, one 3, and one 4. Place them as the base of 4 Foundation piles.
Remove one A, 2, 3, 4; place as base of four foundations. Rest form stock. Turn from stock to foundation or waste.
